questions.stem: For data set 1082, a loop runs with i starting at 0 while i < 15; how many iterations occur?
questions.explanation: The loop continues while i is strictly less than 15. Starting from 0, i takes the values 0 through 14, which is 15 distinct iterations. The strict less-than condition excludes 15 itself, so the count equals the bound.
questions.hint: Count the integer values that satisfy the strict inequality.

questions.stem: For data set 1083, an engineer computes the C expression 5 << 2; what integer results?
questions.explanation: Shifting an integer left by two bit positions multiplies it by four. Therefore 5 << 2 equals 5 times 4, which is 20. A right shift would divide instead, and adding two would be a different operation entirely.
questions.hint: A left shift by n multiplies by two to the power of n.

questions.stem: For data set 1084, a program prints the integer quotient of 134 divided by 7; what appears?
questions.explanation: When both operands are integers, C division discards the fractional part. Dividing 134 by 7 gives a quotient of 19 after truncation. A floating-point divisor would preserve the fraction and give a different result.
questions.hint: Truncate the fractional part of the division result.

questions.stem: For data set 1085, an array of 7 int variables is declared; how many bytes does it occupy if each int is 4 bytes?
questions.explanation: Each int occupies 4 bytes, so 7 of them occupy 7 times 4 = 28 bytes. Remember that an array stores its elements contiguously, so the total is simply the element size multiplied by the element count.
questions.hint: Multiply the element count by the bytes used per element.
